text:
Steven Stamkos spent 16 seasons in Tampa Bay after the Lightning drafted him first overall in 2008, and on Friday night he beat them twice in the same game. He scored on the power play in the third period to pull Nashville level at 4-4, then buried the only shootout goal in the fourth round to give the Predators a 5-4 win over TBL. Nashville trailed in the third and still came out ahead.

The back-and-forth was nonstop. Reid Schaefer opened the scoring, John Carlson answered on a 2% chance (our estimate of how likely that shot was to go in), and Jake Guentzel and Victor Hedman put Tampa Bay up 3-2 before Jayden Struble tied it late in the second. Conor Geekie made it 4-3 early in the third. Nikita Kucherov, drafted 58th overall in 2011, set up three of those goals without taking a shot of note himself.

Underneath, Nashville was the better team. The Predators outshot TBL 33-26 and held a 74-61 edge in shot attempts. Their expected goals, a measure of chance quality, were 3.33 to 2.91, and our simulations say they deserved to win 57% of the time. Neither goalie had a good night by that standard: Justus Annunen allowed 1.1 goals more than his shots warranted, Andrei Vasilevskiy 0.7. The facts here don't include standings or streaks for either club, so we'll leave it at this: Nashville got the extra point it earned, and Tampa Bay left with one it probably didn't.
